sections.name: main
sections.title: Delete one account and related records
sections.what: Looks up one fixed account and, if it exists, deletes its sessions and audit logs before deleting the account itself. It prints a message at each step and reports when the account is missing.
sections.why: Likely reason: a one-off cleanup of a single account. Reason for removing audit logs is not stated.
sections.watch_out: Once the account is deleted there is no undo, and the audit logs removed here cannot be recovered.

summary: A one-time cleanup script that permanently deletes one specific user account along with its sessions and audit logs.
purpose: Removes one account from the database. The code does not state why this account is being removed.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The comments show the author was unsure whether related records would be removed automatically.
how: First it creates a database client and sets a fixed email address. It looks up the account. If the account exists, it deletes that account's sessions, then its audit logs, then the account itself, printing a count or message at each step. If the account does not exist, it prints that. Last it disconnects.
inputs: A hardcoded email address in the file and the database connection setting.
outputs: Permanent deletion of the account and its session and audit records, plus printed messages.
risks: Deletion is permanent and runs immediately with no confirmation step. It removes audit logs, which may be needed to show what happened on the account. Other linked records may block the delete, and the database schema is not in the packet.
debug: If an error mentions a foreign key or constraint, linked rows exist that this script does not remove. Check the schema. Before running again, confirm the account state with the check script.
